---
title: "8 Consensus study"
link-citations: true
---

Alternative labels: among researchers or other interest-holders in health research

## Definition and features
In consensus studies, researchers use Delphi surveys or structured discussion (such as the Nominal Group Technique) to involve researchers and other interest-holders and move them towards a shared position. They usually use a longitudinal design with multiple rounds of feedback, item ratings, or discussions.

- Strengths include the structured synthesis of expert opinion and persuasiveness. 
- Limitations include the dependency of panel composition and process design. 

## Typical purposes and corresponding examples 
[Assess needs and priorities for methods research](../purposes/5assess-needs-priorities.qmd): Delphi study to identify priorities for methods research.[@TudurSmith2014the]

[Develop guidance for understanding and applying methods](../purposes/9guidance-applying.qmd): Guidance on factors to consider when inviting multiple interest-holder groups to research, based on Delphi; [@Parker2022factors] Guidance on handling missing data in trials, based on Nominal Group Technique.[@Hussain2022development]

[Develop reporting guidelines](../purposes/10guidance-reporting.qmd): Delphi study to develop CONSORT reporting guideline.[@Hopewell2025consort] 

[Develop quality assessment instruments](../purposes/11guidance-assessing.qmd): Discussion-based consensus on quality assessment tool for subgroup analyses.[@Schandelmaier2020development]
